encryption.description: Upgrade at-rest encryption to SSE-KMS. Set to "kms" to enable. SSE-S3 (AES256) is always on by default at no cost. SSE-KMS incurs KMS API call cost and is required by HIPAA, PCI-DSS, FedRAMP, and IRAP.

logging.description: Enable S3 server access logging to the centralised logging bucket created during `anvil bootstrap`. Required by most compliance frameworks for audit trails. Incurs storage cost. Default: false.

retention.description: Enable Object Lock with a retention period in days (COMPLIANCE mode). Objects cannot be deleted or overwritten until the period expires. Required by PCI-DSS (365), FedRAMP (1095), HIPAA (2190). Must be set at bucket creation — changing requires bucket replacement. Default: 0 (disabled).

storageTransition.description: When to move objects to cheaper storage classes. Omit to use Intelligent-Tiering (recommended default). Only applies when no custom lifecycle is provided via hatch.

enum.description: Standard → IA at 30 days, Glacier at 90 days
Standard → IA at 90 days, Glacier at 365 days
Standard → IA at 365 days, Glacier at 730 days

versionRetention.description: How long non-current object versions are kept before automatic expiry. Strongly recommended when versioning is enabled to prevent unbounded storage growth. Default: keep forever.

versioning.description: Enable versioning in non-production stages. Versioning is always enabled in production. Incurs additional storage cost per version. Default: false.

arn.description: The ARN of the S3 bucket.

bucketName.description: The name of the S3 bucket.

anvil:aws:CognitoAuth.description: An Anvil-managed JWT authorizer backed by a Cognito user pool. Derives the issuer URL automatically from the user pool ID — no manual Cognito endpoint construction required. Configures a native API Gateway JWT authorizer (created by the HttpApi it is attached to); verification is handled entirely by API Gateway with no Lambda or custom code. Pass authorizerId to HttpApi defaultAuthorizerId to protect your API routes.

audience.description: The Cognito app client IDs allowed to access this API. API Gateway rejects tokens whose 'aud' claim does not match one of these values. Pass your Cognito app client ID(s) here.

userPoolId.description: The Cognito user pool ID. Pass pool.userPoolId directly. Accepts Output<string>. Anvil derives the issuer URL automatically: https://cognito-idp.{region}.amazonaws.com/{userPoolId}.

authorizerId.description: Reference to this authorizer's JWT configuration. Pass this to HttpApi defaultAuthorizerId — HttpApi creates the API Gateway authorizer on its own API, since authorizers can't be shared across APIs.

anvil:aws:CognitoUserPool.description: An Anvil-managed Cognito user pool. Tier 1 controls (deletion protection, enforced password policy, account recovery via email) are always on. Pair with CognitoAuth to protect API Gateway routes.

appClient.description: Default app client created with the user pool. Covers the 80% case of one application per pool. Use hatch for additional clients.

attributes.description: User attribute configuration. Controls sign-in identifiers and required attributes on sign-up.

emailConfiguration.description: Email delivery configuration. Default: Cognito-managed email (5 emails/day limit). Set sesFromAddress for SES delivery in production.

hostedUi.description: Hosted UI / Managed Login configuration. Omit to use the Cognito user pools API directly without a hosted sign-in page.

identityProviders.description: External identity providers to federate with this user pool. Supports Google, Facebook, LoginWithAmazon, SignInWithApple, OIDC, and SAML. Schema never changes per provider — add new providers by extending this array.

mfa.description: MFA configuration. TOTP requires no additional AWS resources. SMS requires an SNS caller ARN.

passwordPolicy.description: Password policy for the user pool. Anvil enforces a secure baseline by default — override only to strengthen.

waf.description: Attaches a regional WAF WebACL to the user pool. AWS recommends a WAF for every public user pool — it protects sign-in and sign-up against credential stuffing, brute force, bots and SMS pumping. Use an Anvil Waf created with scope "regional" in the same region as the pool.

appClientId.description: The ID of the default app client. Pass to CognitoAuth audience.

appClientSecret.description: The client secret of the default app client. Only populated when appClient.generateSecret is true. Treat as sensitive.

cloudFrontDomain.description: The CloudFront distribution domain for the custom hosted UI. Only populated when hostedUi.customDomain is true. Create a Route53 alias record pointing hostedUi.domain to this value to complete DNS setup. Empty string for Cognito-managed domains.

endpoint.description: The Cognito OIDC issuer URL. Format: https://cognito-idp.{region}.amazonaws.com/{userPoolId}. Pass directly to CognitoAuth if building the authorizer manually.

hostedUiDomain.description: The full hosted UI domain (e.g. https://auth.myapp.com or https://myprefix.auth.us-east-1.amazoncognito.com). Empty string if hostedUi is not configured.

userPoolArn.description: The ARN of the Cognito user pool.

userPoolId.description: The Cognito user pool ID. Pass to CognitoAuth.userPoolId.

anvil:aws:ComplianceScanner.description: Internal: created by App when `compliance` is set. Schedules this app's Prowler compliance scans on the shared Anvil scanner. Do not construct directly — set `compliance` on your App instead.

cron.description: Six AWS cron fields (minutes hours day-of-month month day-of-week year), used when schedule is cron. At most once an hour.

frameworks.description: Frameworks to scan against: friendly names (soc2, iso27001, cis, nist-800-53, nist-800-171, nist-csf, pci, hipaa, fsbp, gdpr, nis2, dora, fedramp-low, fedramp-moderate, cmmc, essential-eight, well-architected, c5, csa-ccm) or any raw Prowler AWS compliance ID.

regions.description: Regions the app deploys to, in addition to the provider's region. us-east-1 is always scanned for global services.

retention.description: How long scan results are kept: 30d, 90d, 180d, 1y (default), 2y, 7y.

scanOnDeploy.description: Start a scan after each successful deploy. Default: false.

schedule.description: When to scan: daily (default), weekly, none, or cron (with `cron`). Presets run at a fixed time derived from the project and stage, so apps in one account don't all scan at once.

timezone.description: IANA time zone for the schedule, e.g. Australia/Sydney. Default: UTC.

scheduleExpression.description: The EventBridge Scheduler expression. Empty when schedule is none.

scheduleName.description: The schedule's name in the anvil-compliance schedule group. Empty when schedule is none.

anvil:aws:DSQL.description: Serverless distributed PostgreSQL-compatible database. Secure-by-default Aurora DSQL cluster with optional multi-region active-active replication, IAM authentication, deploy-time role bootstrapping, and AWS Backup integration. No VPC required — connect directly via IAM auth tokens.

backup.description: AWS Backup configuration. Omit to disable. When set, Anvil opts in the DSQL resource type per region, creates a backup plan with retention and schedule, and for multi-region clusters automatically adds cross-region copy rules.

multiRegion.description: Opt-in multi-region configuration. When set, Anvil creates two clusters in the specified regions and links them via ClusterPeering. When omitted, a single-region cluster is created in the provider's default region.

schemas.description: Schemas and the tables within them. Anvil creates each schema and table (additive-only — new tables/columns/indexes are applied; removals are left to humans). Omit to skip table management.

stream.description: Sends the cluster's change data capture (CDC) events, every committed row change in every table, to a Kinesis Data Stream. Anvil creates the IAM role DSQL writes with; `anvil deploy` creates the CDC stream after the rest of the stack, and `anvil destroy` deletes it first. Removing it deletes the CDC stream, and changes made while it's gone are never captured. Omit to keep CDC off.

vpc.description: Optional VPC configuration. When set without hasNat, Anvil creates interface VPC endpoints (PrivateLink) per region so traffic stays on the AWS backbone. When omitted, the Lambda connects to the public DSQL endpoint over the internet using IAM auth tokens over TLS.

clusterArns.description: Map of region to cluster ARN. Single-region: one entry. Multi-region: one entry per region. e.g. { "us-east-1": "arn:aws:dsql:us-east-1:..." }.

endpoint.description: The single cluster endpoint for the provider's default region. Convenience for the common single-region case — pass straight to a Lambda env var: { DSQL_ENDPOINT: dsql.endpoint }. For multi-region this is the local-region endpoint; use endpoints[region] for another.

endpoints.description: Map of region to cluster endpoint. Single-region: one entry keyed by the provider region. Multi-region: one entry per region. e.g. { "us-east-1": "abc123.dsql.us-east-1.on.aws" }. Pass the relevant endpoint to your Lambda via environment variables.

rolesTableName.description: DynamoDB table name for role bootstrap. Passed to DSQLConnect (via grantConnect) so it can create the IAM role-mapping item. Empty when no roles are configured.

streamKinesisArn.description: The Kinesis stream CDC events are sent to. Empty when stream is omitted.

streamRoleArn.description: The IAM role DSQL writes CDC events with: the one Anvil created, or stream.roleArn. Empty when stream is omitted.

vpcEndpointIds.description: Map of region to VPC endpoint ID. Only populated when vpc is set and hasNat is false. Pass to LambdaVpcEndpointArgs.endpointId.

vpcEndpointSecurityGroupIds.description: Map of region to VPC endpoint security group ID. Only populated when vpc is set and hasNat is false. Pass to LambdaVpcEndpointArgs.securityGroupId: the SG allows its members to reach the endpoint on port 5432, so joining it is what gives the Lambda network access.

anvil:aws:DSQLConnect.description: Grants a compute resource (Lambda, ECS, etc.) connect access to an Anvil DSQL cluster. Creates the IAM policy (dsql:DbConnect) and optionally a DynamoDB IAM mapping item that triggers the bootstrap Lambda to run AWS IAM GRANT, mapping the compute resource's IAM role to a Postgres database role.

clusterArns.description: Map of region to cluster ARN from the DSQL component. Used to scope the dsql:DbConnect IAM policy.

dbRoles.description: Postgres database role names to map this IAM identity to. One mapping is created per role; the bootstrap Lambda runs AWS IAM GRANT "<role>" TO 'arn:...' for each. The compute connects as whichever role it chooses at runtime.

rolesTableName.description: DynamoDB table name for role bootstrap. Pass dsql.rolesTableName from the DSQL component. When set with dbRole, a TableItem is created to trigger the bootstrap Lambda. Optional — omit when roles are not configured.

targetName.description: Logical name of the compute resource. Used for naming child resources.

targetRoleArn.description: IAM execution role ARN of the compute resource (Lambda, ECS task, etc.) that will connect to the cluster.

anvil:aws:DynamoDB.description: Serverless key-value and document store. Secure-by-default DynamoDB table with GSI support, optional streams, and Lambda/EventBridge consumers. First data layer component — pairs naturally with anvil.aws.Lambda.

globalSecondaryIndexes.description: Global Secondary Indexes. All GSI key types must be explicitly declared — Anvil derives attributeDefinitions automatically from all declared keys.

kmsKeyArn.description: Tier 2 opt-in. ARN of a KMS CMK for encryption at rest. If omitted, AWS_OWNED_KMS is used (Tier 1 default — always on, zero cost). Use this for compliance workloads requiring key rotation control, audit trail, or the ability to revoke access by disabling the key.

stream.description: DynamoDB Streams configuration. Opt-in. Enables change data capture on the table.

ttlAttribute.description: Name of the attribute used for TTL (time-to-live). Items with this attribute set to a past Unix timestamp are automatically deleted by DynamoDB.

streamArn.description: The ARN of the DynamoDB stream. Only present when stream is enabled.

tableArn.description: The ARN of the DynamoDB table.

tableName.description: The physical DynamoDB table name. Scoped as {name}-{stage}.

anvil:aws:EventBus.description: An Anvil-managed EventBridge event bus. Archives events for 7 days by default for replay and debugging. Rules route matching events to Lambda targets.

rules.description: EventBridge rules on this bus. Each rule matches events by pattern and routes them to a target.

arn.description: The ARN of the EventBridge event bus.

name.description: The name of the EventBridge event bus. Pass to HttpApi consumer: { eventBridge: { name: bus.name } }

anvil:aws:HttpApi.description: An Anvil-managed AWS HTTP API Gateway (API Gateway v2). Route-level consumers support Lambda, SQS, EventBridge, Step Functions, and HTTP proxy integrations. Secure by default: TLS 1.2 minimum enforced on custom domains, execute-api endpoint disabled when a custom domain is set, conservative throttling defaults (1000 rps / 500 burst), CORS opt-in with wildcard origin blocked, per-consumer least-privilege IAM roles, access logs on by default.

cors.description: Optional CORS configuration. Opt-in — omit to disable CORS entirely. When enabled, allowOrigins is required and wildcard '*' is blocked as a security measure.

defaultAuthorizerId.description: JWT authorizer to apply to all routes — HttpApi creates it on this API. Pass auth.authorizerId from an OAuthAuthorizer or CognitoAuth component. All routes inherit this authorizer unless skipAuth: true is set on the route. Omit to leave all routes public.

domain.description: Optional custom domain for the API. When set, Anvil provisions the ACM certificate, API Gateway domain name, and Route 53 DNS record automatically. The raw execute-api endpoint is disabled — all traffic must flow through the custom domain.

logRetention.description: CloudWatch access log retention period. Presets: '7d' | '30d' | '90d' | '1y' | '3y' | '6y' | '7y'. Default: '1y' — satisfies SOC 2, ISO 27001, and PCI DSS baseline retention requirements.

routes.description: The API routes. Each route maps a method and path to a consumer. At least one route is required.

throttling.description: Optional throttling configuration. Defaults to rateLimit: 1000 rps and burstLimit: 500 concurrent requests when omitted. Without throttling a single route can exhaust the account-level limit shared across all APIs.

apiEndpoint.description: The default execute-api endpoint URL. Empty string when a custom domain is set and the execute-api endpoint is disabled.

apiId.description: The API Gateway HTTP API ID.

certValidationCname.description: ACM cert validation CNAME. Only populated when domain.dns: false and domain.certificateArn is omitted. Add this record in Cloudflare (or your DNS provider) then re-run deploy — Anvil blocks until ACM confirms validation.

url.description: The primary URL for the API. When a custom domain is configured this is the custom domain URL. Otherwise it is the execute-api endpoint URL.

anvil:aws:KinesisStream.description: An Anvil-managed Kinesis Data Stream. On-demand capacity by default (set provisioned for a fixed shard count), and server-side encryption with the AWS-managed KMS key (alias/aws/kinesis) is always on. Add Lambda consumers with consumers (each gets a dead letter queue and safe retry defaults); use grantRead/grantWrite for other compute.

consumers.description: Lambda functions that read the stream. Each consumer gets an event source mapping (starting from the oldest record, bisect-on-error, 3 retries), its own dead letter queue for records that still fail, sqs:SendMessage on that DLQ, and — with grantRead: true — the grantRead permissions. All consumers share the stream's read throughput (2 MB/s per shard). Each consumer's resources are named after its consumerName, so adding, removing or reordering consumers only touches the one that changed.

maxRecordSizeKib.description: Largest record the stream accepts, in KiB, 1024–10240. Default: 2048, so the stream can take Aurora DSQL CDC events (rows up to 2 MiB) without extra config.

provisioned.description: Switches the stream from on-demand to provisioned capacity with a fixed shard count. When omitted, the stream is on-demand and scales shards automatically with traffic — the right choice unless throughput is steady and predictable.

retentionHours.description: How long records stay readable, in hours, 24–8760 (365 days). Default: 24. Retention beyond 24 hours is billed separately.

arn.description: The ARN of the Kinesis stream.

dlqArns.description: Each consumer's consumerName mapped to the ARN of its dead letter queue.

dlqUrls.description: Each consumer's consumerName mapped to the URL of its dead letter queue.

name.description: The physical name of the Kinesis stream.

encryption.description: Upgrade environment variable encryption to SSE-KMS. Set to "kms" to enable. Incurs KMS API call cost. Required by HIPAA, PCI-DSS, FedRAMP. Supply kmsKeyArn via hatch["lambda"].

environment.description: Environment variables available to the function at runtime. Supports plain strings and Pulumi outputs.

handler.description: Where the function's code is, relative to the project root, in the usual Lambda form. Node: <file without extension>.<export>, e.g. "functions/api/index.handler" for `export const handler` in functions/api/index.ts; omit to deploy a blank placeholder. Rust (required): a Cargo package directory or a .rs file, e.g. "functions/api".

logRetention.description: CloudWatch log group retention period. Default: "1y" (satisfies SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS baseline).

memory.description: Memory in MB. Valid: 128 to 32768 in 1MB increments. Default: 1024.

permissions.description: Inline IAM permissions added to the execution role. Use for ad-hoc access not covered by the grant system.

runtime.description: The Lambda runtime. "rust" deploys a Rust function on the OS-only provided.al2023 runtime and requires entry.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds. Valid: 1 to 900. Default: 5.

tracing.description: Enable AWS X-Ray tracing. Incurs per-trace cost (~$5/million traces). Default: false.

url.description: Enable a direct HTTPS endpoint for the function. Auth mode is AWS_IAM - never public. Default: false.

vpc.description: Places the Lambda inside a VPC for access to private resources such as RDS or ElastiCache. Anvil creates a dedicated security group with zero inbound and zero outbound rules. Nothing is reachable until explicitly granted via the grant system.

arn.description: The ARN of the Lambda function.

functionName.description: The physical name of the Lambda function.

functionUrl.description: The HTTPS endpoint URL when url: true. Empty string if URL is not enabled.

roleArn.description: The ARN of the Lambda's IAM execution role.

securityGroupId.description: The ID of the dedicated security group created for this Lambda. Only populated when vpc is set. Use this to grant other resources access to this Lambda via the grant system.

anvil:aws:OAuthAuthorizer.description: An Anvil-managed JWT authorizer for HTTP API Gateway. Works with any OIDC-compliant identity provider — Auth0, Clerk, Google, Okta, Cognito. API Gateway verifies the JWT signature, issuer, audience, and expiry on every request natively — no Lambda or custom code required. Pass authorizerId to HttpApi defaultAuthorizerId to protect your routes.

audience.description: The intended recipients of the JWT. API Gateway rejects tokens whose 'aud' claim does not match one of these values. For Auth0 this is the API identifier (e.g. 'https://api.myapp.com'), not the application client ID.

issuer.description: The OIDC issuer URL of your identity provider. API Gateway fetches public signing keys from {issuer}/.well-known/jwks.json to verify token signatures. Examples: Auth0: 'https://your-tenant.auth0.com/', Clerk: 'https://your-instance.clerk.accounts.dev', Google: 'https://accounts.google.com'.

authorizerId.description: Reference to this authorizer's JWT configuration. Pass this to HttpApi defaultAuthorizerId — HttpApi creates the API Gateway authorizer on its own API, since authorizers can't be shared across APIs.

anvil:aws:Queue.description: An Anvil-managed SQS queue. A dead letter queue is always provisioned to prevent silent message loss. SSE-SQS encryption is enabled by default at no cost.

consumer.description: Wires a compute resource to consume messages from this queue. Creates the event source mapping (trigger) and grants the necessary IAM permissions automatically.

dlq.description: Dead letter queue configuration. Always provisioned — messages that fail processing are moved here instead of being silently dropped. Omit to use defaults (managed DLQ, maxReceiveCount: 3). Set arn to reuse an existing queue.

fifo.description: Creates a FIFO queue when true. FIFO queues guarantee message ordering and exactly-once processing but have lower throughput (~3,000 msg/s vs unlimited for standard). Use for financial transactions, inventory updates, or any workflow where ordering or deduplication matters. Default: false.

arn.description: The ARN of the SQS queue.

dlqArn.description: The ARN of the dead letter queue.

dlqUrl.description: The URL of the dead letter queue.

name.description: The physical name of the SQS queue.

url.description: The URL of the SQS queue. Use this to send and receive messages.

environment.description: Environment vars available at BOTH build time and runtime. Values must be string literals since they're needed before the build runs.

originProtection.description: OriginProtection locks CloudFront to a CDN/proxy in front of it (Cloudflare, Fastly, Akamai, nginx, ...). Requests without the x-origin-secret header are rejected at the edge; configure the proxy to send it on every request with the originSecret output as the value. Protection defaults to "edge-oac" while it's enabled, so the server Function URL can't be reached around the proxy.

protection.description: Protection controls who can invoke the server Lambda's Function URL. Default: "none", or "edge-oac" while a WAF is attached or origin protection is enabled. An explicit value always wins. "none": public Function URL; anyone who learns it can call the server directly, bypassing CloudFront. "oac": locked to CloudFront via IAM; requests with a body are rejected unless they already carry an x-amz-content-sha256 header. "edge-oac": "oac" plus a Lambda@Edge function that adds the header, following AWS's guidance — nothing is needed in the app; request bodies over 1 MB are rejected. In "oac" and "edge-oac", a viewer Authorization header is replaced by CloudFront's signature.

runtimeEnvironment.description: Runtime-only environment vars set on the Lambda function. Supports Pulumi Output values (e.g. bucket.name, fn.arn). Only available at request time, NOT during build/prerendering.

securityHeaders.description: SecurityHeaders configures the security headers CloudFront adds to every response. On by default: Strict-Transport-Security (1 year), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, a Permissions-Policy that turns off camera, microphone, geolocation, USB and Topics, and Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin-allow-popups. Headers your app sets itself take priority. Content-Security-Policy is left to SvelteKit's kit.csp.

waf.description: Waf attaches a WAF WebACL to the site's CloudFront distribution. Protection defaults to "edge-oac" while it's attached.

originSecret.description: OriginSecret is the x-origin-secret header value to configure in the CDN/proxy. Secret. Stable across deploys. Only populated when originProtection is enabled.

availabilityZones.description: Number of Availability Zones to deploy subnets into. Valid values: 1, 2, 3. Defaults to 1. Inherits from App.defaults.availability — 'high' maps to 3, 'low' maps to 1.

bastion.description: Optional SSM bastion host for private network access. No SSH, no port 22 — access via AWS SSM Session Manager only. Use to connect to RDS, ElastiCache, and other private resources locally.

cidr.description: The IPv4 CIDR block for the VPC. Default: '10.0.0.0/16'. Public subnets carved from offset 0 (/24 each), private subnets from offset 10 (/24 each).

flowLogs.description: Optional VPC Flow Log configuration. Opt-in only. Either or both destinations can be enabled simultaneously. CloudWatch for active debugging, S3 for long-term compliance retention.

nat.description: Optional NAT configuration for outbound internet access from private subnets. Omit for a fully private VPC.

availabilityZones.description: The resolved Availability Zone names, e.g. ['ap-southeast-2a']. Consumed by RDS Multi-AZ, ECS spread, and other downstream components.

bastionInstanceId.description: The EC2 instance ID of the bastion host. Use with: aws ssm start-session --target <bastionInstanceId>. Only populated when bastion is enabled.

bastionSecurityGroupId.description: The security group ID of the bastion host. Use to grant the bastion access to private resources, e.g. db.grant(network.bastion, { access: 'readWrite' }). Only populated when bastion is enabled.

defaultSecurityGroupId.description: The ID of the VPC default security group. All rules removed — not used by Anvil components.

privateSubnetIds.description: The IDs of the private subnets, one per AZ. Used by Lambda, ECS tasks, EC2, and RDS.

publicSubnetIds.description: The IDs of the public subnets, one per AZ. Used by load balancers, NAT Gateways, and the bastion host.

anvil:aws:VpcEndpoint.description: An Anvil-managed AWS Interface VPC Endpoint. Creates one ENI per private subnet with private DNS enabled. The endpoint security group uses a self-referencing ingress rule on port 443 — only compute resources that have been explicitly granted access can reach the endpoint at the network layer. Access is enforced at three layers: network (self-referencing SG), IAM role policy (scoped per compute resource), and endpoint policy (blanket ceiling on allowed actions for all compute principals — Lambda, ECS, EC2).

overridePermissions.description: Explicit Allow and Deny permission statements for the endpoint policy. When omitted, the endpoint policy allows all actions (*) for all Anvil compute principals (Lambda, ECS, EC2). When set, only the declared actions are permitted — the caller is responsible for declaring every action their compute resources need. Supports both Allow and Deny effects. Resource defaults to "*" if omitted on a permission entry.

privateSubnetIds.description: The IDs of the private subnets to attach the endpoint to. AWS places one ENI per subnet. Pass all private subnet IDs from your VPC — typically one per AZ.

service.description: The AWS service to route privately. The full com.amazonaws.{region}.{service} name is constructed at deploy time from the resolved region — you never write it manually.

vpcId.description: The ID of the VPC to create the endpoint in. Accepts both Anvil-managed VPC IDs and imported VPC IDs.

dnsName.description: The first DNS name assigned to the endpoint, e.g. vpce-xxx.sqs.ap-southeast-2.vpce.amazonaws.com. With private DNS enabled, normal consumers use the standard AWS SDK hostname — this is exposed for debugging and multi-VPC architectures only.

endpointId.description: The ID of the VPC endpoint, e.g. vpce-0abc1234567890abc. Use this to reference the endpoint in IAM condition keys such as aws:SourceVpce.

securityGroupId.description: The ID of the dedicated security group attached to this endpoint. Uses a self-referencing ingress rule on port 443 — only compute resources with this SG explicitly attached can reach the endpoint at the network layer.

anvil:aws:Waf.description: An Anvil-managed AWS WAF WebACL with researched defaults: a per-client rate limit (2000 requests / 5 min) and AWS managed rule groups for IP reputation, known bad inputs, the OWASP core rule set and SQL injection. Starts in count mode — matches are logged, not blocked — until mode is set to "block". Attach it to a site with waf: { arn } or to a Cognito user pool with waf: { arn }.

blockCountries.description: Two-letter ISO 3166 country codes to block, e.g. ["KP"]. Follows mode.

clientIpHeader.description: Header carrying the real visitor IP when the site sits behind a proxy, e.g. "CF-Connecting-IP" for Cloudflare. The rate limit, IP lists and country blocking then use the visitor's IP instead of the proxy's. AWS's ipReputation and anonymousIp rule groups can't read this header, so they default to off when it's set.

ipAllowList.description: IP addresses or CIDRs (IPv4 and IPv6) that are always allowed, skipping every other rule — e.g. office networks or uptime monitors.

ipBlockList.description: IP addresses or CIDRs (IPv4 and IPv6) that are always blocked.

logging.description: Logging to CloudWatch Logs. On by default: blocked and counted requests only, kept 30 days, with the authorization, cookie and x-origin-secret headers redacted.

managedRules.description: AWS managed rule groups. On by default: core, knownBadInputs, ipReputation, sqli. Off by default: anonymousIp, adminProtection.

mode.description: What rules do when they match. "count" (default): log the match without blocking — use this to check for false positives on live traffic. "block": block matching requests. The IP allow and block lists always allow / block regardless of mode.

rateLimit.description: Per-client rate limit. On by default: 2000 requests per client per 5 minutes.

ruleOverrides.description: Override the action of individual AWS managed rules, keyed by exact AWS rule name: "count", "block" or "allow". Default: { SizeRestrictions_BODY: "count" } — that rule blocks any body over 8 KB, which breaks forms, JSON APIs and uploads. Set it to "block" to restore it.

scope.description: What the WAF protects. "cloudfront" (default): sites and other CloudFront distributions; created in us-east-1 as AWS requires. "regional": regional resources such as Cognito user pools; created in the stack's region.

arn.description: The WebACL ARN. Pass it to a site's waf.arn (cloudfront scope) or a Cognito user pool's waf.arn (regional scope).

logGroupName.description: The CloudWatch log group receiving WAF logs. Empty when logging is off.

name.description: The physical WebACL name.

entryPoint.description: The name of the function to execute.

location.description: The GCP region to deploy to (e.g. us-central1).

name.description: The name of the Cloud Function.

runtime.description: The runtime to use (e.g. nodejs20, python312, go122).

dataClassification.description: Data classification level for the bucket.

location.description: The GCS location (e.g. US, EU, us-central1).

expectedBucketOwner.deprecationMessage: expected_bucket_owner is deprecated. It will be removed in a future verion of the provider.
expectedBucketOwner.description: Account ID of the expected bucket owner.

region.description: Region where this resource will be [managed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#regional-endpoints). Defaults to the Region set in the provider configuration.

status.description: Transfer acceleration state of the bucket. Valid values: `Enabled`, `Suspended`.

accessControlPolicy.description: Configuration block that sets the ACL permissions for an object per grantee. See below.

arn.description: ARN of an existing queue to use as the DLQ. If the parent queue is fifo: true, this ARN must end with ".fifo". When omitted, Anvil creates a managed DLQ.

maxReceiveCount.description: How many times a message can be received before being moved to the DLQ. Default: 3.

anvil:aws:QueueLambdaConsumerArgs.description: Lambda consumer configuration. Pass fn.arn and fn.roleArn from an Anvil Lambda component.

arn.description: The ARN of the Lambda function to trigger. Use fn.arn from an Anvil Lambda component.

lambdaRoleArn.description: The ARN of the Lambda's execution role. Use fn.roleArn from an Anvil Lambda component. Required for Anvil to attach the consume permissions policy.

contentBasedDeduplication.description: Enables content-based deduplication for FIFO queues. For more information, see the [related documentation](http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/FIFO-queues.html#FIFO-queues-exactly-once-processing).

deduplicationScope.description: Specifies whether message deduplication occurs at the message group or queue level. Valid values are `messageGroup` and `queue` (default).

delaySeconds.description: Time in seconds that the delivery of all messages in the queue will be delayed. An integer from 0 to 900 (15 minutes). The default for this attribute is 0 seconds.

fifoQueue.description: Boolean designating a FIFO queue. If not set, it defaults to `false` making it standard.

fifoThroughputLimit.description: Specifies whether the FIFO queue throughput quota applies to the entire queue or per message group. Valid values are `perQueue` (default) and `perMessageGroupId`.

kmsDataKeyReusePeriodSeconds.description: Length of time, in seconds, for which Amazon SQS can reuse a data key to encrypt or decrypt messages before calling AWS KMS again. An integer representing seconds, between 60 seconds (1 minute) and 86,400 seconds (24 hours). The default is 300 (5 minutes).

kmsMasterKeyId.description: ID of an AWS-managed customer master key (CMK) for Amazon SQS or a custom CMK. For more information, see [Key Terms](http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-server-side-encryption.html#sqs-sse-key-terms).

maxMessageSize.description: Limit of how many bytes a message can contain before Amazon SQS rejects it. An integer from 1024 bytes (1 KiB) up to 1048576 bytes (1024 KiB). The default for this attribute is 262144 (256 KiB).

messageRetentionSeconds.description: Number of seconds Amazon SQS retains a message. Integer representing seconds, from 60 (1 minute) to 1209600 (14 days). The default for this attribute is 345600 (4 days).

name.description: Name of the queue. Queue names must be made up of only uppercase and lowercase ASCII letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens, and must be between 1 and 80 characters long. For a FIFO (first-in-first-out) queue, the name must end with the `.fifo` suffix. If omitted, the provider will assign a random, unique name. Conflicts with `name_prefix`.

namePrefix.description: Creates a unique name beginning with the specified prefix. Conflicts with `name`.

policy.description: JSON policy for the SQS queue. For more information about building AWS IAM policy documents see the AWS IAM Policy Document Guide. The provider will only perform drift detection of its value when present in a configuration. It is preferred to use the `aws.sqs.QueuePolicy` resource instead.

receiveWaitTimeSeconds.description: Time for which a ReceiveMessage call will wait for a message to arrive (long polling) before returning. An integer from 0 to 20 (seconds). The default for this attribute is 0, meaning that the call will return immediately.

redriveAllowPolicy.description: JSON policy to set up the Dead Letter Queue redrive permission, see [AWS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/SQSDeadLetterQueue.html). The provider will only perform drift detection of its value when present in a configuration. It is preferred to use the `aws.sqs.RedriveAllowPolicy` resource instead.

redrivePolicy.description: JSON policy to set up the Dead Letter Queue, see [AWS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/SQSDeadLetterQueue.html). The provider will only perform drift detection of its value when present in a configuration. It is preferred to use the `aws.sqs.RedrivePolicy` resource instead. **Note:** when specifying `maxReceiveCount`, you must specify it as an integer (`5`), and not a string (`"5"`).

region.description: Region where this resource will be [managed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#regional-endpoints). Defaults to the Region set in the provider configuration.

sqsManagedSseEnabled.description: Boolean to enable server-side encryption (SSE) of message content with SQS-owned encryption keys. See [Encryption at rest](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-server-side-encryption.html). The provider will only perform drift detection of its value when present in a configuration.

tags.description: Map of tags to assign to the queue. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.

visibilityTimeoutSeconds.description: Visibility timeout for the queue. An integer from 0 to 43200 (12 hours). The default for this attribute is 30. For more information about visibility timeout, see [AWS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/AboutVT.html).

enum.description: Auto-tiered: Standard (0-30d) → Standard-IA (30-90d) → Glacier Instant Retrieval (90d+). Suitable for compliance retention at minimal long-term cost.

anvil:aws:SiteCrossOriginOpenerPolicy.description: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: isolates the site's browser window from windows on other sites. Default: "same-origin-allow-popups".

enum.description: Isolated from other sites, but popups it opens (OAuth sign-in, payments) still work. Default.
enum.name: SameOriginAllowPopups

enum.description: Strict isolation. Breaks sign-in and payment popups that report back to the page.
enum.name: SameOrigin

anvil:aws:SiteFrameOptions.description: Whether other sites can embed this one in a frame (X-Frame-Options). Default: "sameorigin".

enum.description: Only pages on this site can frame it. Default.
enum.name: Sameorigin

enum.description: No site can frame it, including this one.
enum.name: Deny

enum.description: No X-Frame-Options header — any site can embed it. Use only for sites meant to be embedded elsewhere.
enum.name: None

anvil:aws:SiteHsts.description: SiteHstsArgs configures optional Strict-Transport-Security directives. Both are hard to undo — browsers remember them for the max-age (1 year).

includeSubDomains.description: IncludeSubDomains applies HSTS to every subdomain of the site's domain. Default: false.

preload.description: Preload marks the domain as eligible for browsers' built-in HSTS preload list. Requires includeSubDomains. Default: false.

anvil:aws:SiteProtection.description: Who can invoke the site's server Lambda Function URL. Default: "none", or "edge-oac" while a WAF is attached or origin protection is enabled. An explicit value always wins.

enum.description: Public Function URL. Anyone who learns it can call the server directly, bypassing CloudFront and any WAF or proxy.
enum.name: None

enum.description: Locked to CloudFront via IAM + OAC. Requests with a body are rejected unless they already carry an x-amz-content-sha256 header.
enum.name: Oac

enum.description: Locked to CloudFront via IAM + OAC, with a Lambda@Edge function that adds the x-amz-content-sha256 header (AWS's documented approach). Nothing is needed in the app; request bodies over 1 MB are rejected.
enum.name: EdgeOac

anvil:aws:SiteSecurityHeaders.description: SiteSecurityHeadersArgs configures the security headers CloudFront adds to every response. On by default: Strict-Transport-Security (1 year), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, a Permissions-Policy that turns off camera, microphone, geolocation, USB and Topics, and Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin-allow-popups. A header your app sets itself always takes priority. Content-Security-Policy is not set — configure it in the framework (e.g. SvelteKit's kit.csp).

crossOriginOpenerPolicy.description: CrossOriginOpenerPolicy isolates the site's browser window from windows on other sites. "same-origin-allow-popups" (default): isolated, but popups it opens (OAuth sign-in, payments) still work. "same-origin": strict isolation — breaks sign-in and payment popups that report back. "none": no Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header.

enabled.description: Enabled turns the security headers on or off. Default: true.

frameOptions.description: FrameOptions controls whether other sites can embed this one in a frame. "sameorigin" (default): only pages on this site. "deny": never. "none": no X-Frame-Options header — the site can be embedded anywhere.

permissionsPolicy.description: PermissionsPolicy is the Permissions-Policy header value: which browser features the site (and anything it embeds) may use. Default: "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), usb=(), browsing-topics=()". Set your own value to allow a feature, e.g. "camera=(self), microphone=(self)", or "none" to send no Permissions-Policy header.

anvil:aws:SiteWaf.description: SiteWafArgs attaches a WAF to the site. Composes freely with originProtection. While a WAF is attached, protection defaults to "edge-oac" so the server Function URL can't be used to bypass the WAF.

arn.description: Arn is the ARN of a WAF WebACL with CLOUDFRONT scope (us-east-1). Pass waf.arn from an Anvil Waf component.

allowedCidrs.description: Source IP CIDRs allowed to initiate SSM sessions via IAM policy condition. Omit to allow any authenticated IAM principal. Example: ['203.0.113.0/32'] to restrict to your office IP.

instanceType.description: EC2 instance type for the bastion host. Default: 't4g.nano' — the bastion is purely a jump box with minimal resource requirements.

retention.description: Number of days to retain flow log data in CloudWatch Logs. Common values: 7, 14, 30, 90.

anvil:aws:VpcEndpointPermission.description: A single permission statement in the VPC endpoint policy. Effect must be Allow or Deny. Action is an IAM action string. Resource defaults to * if omitted.

resource.description: The ARN to scope this permission to. Defaults to "*" if omitted — applies to all resources of this service. Accepts Output<string> — pass resource ARNs directly, e.g. queue.arn, secret.arn.

cloudwatch.description: Enable flow log delivery to a CloudWatch Log Group. Use for fast querying with CloudWatch Logs Insights and active debugging of connection issues.

s3.description: Enable flow log delivery to a dedicated S3 bucket with auto-tiered lifecycle policy. Use for compliance retention and audit evidence.

privateSubnetIds.description: IDs of the private subnets. If omitted, auto-discovered by inspecting route tables — private subnets have no route to an Internet Gateway.

publicSubnetIds.description: IDs of the public subnets. If omitted, auto-discovered by inspecting route tables — public subnets have a default route to an Internet Gateway.

vpcId.description: The ID of the existing VPC to import. Anvil does not manage, modify, or own the imported VPC.

instanceType.description: EC2 instance type for the fck-nat instance. Only applies when natType is 'fck-nat'. Default: 't4g.small'.

natType.description: Type of NAT to provision. 'gateway' provisions one AWS managed NAT Gateway per AZ. 'fck-nat' provisions a single fck-nat EC2 instance shared across all AZs.

enum.description: AWS managed NAT Gateway. One per AZ for true HA. ~$32/month per AZ plus $0.045/GB data processed.
fck-nat EC2 instance. Single instance regardless of AZ count. ~$4-6/month for t4g.small. Accepted single point of failure tradeoff for cost savings.

lifecycle.description: Storage tiering policy for flow log retention.

enabled.description: Turns logging on or off. Default: true.

includeAllowed.description: Also log allowed requests. Default: false — only blocked and counted requests, which keeps cost low.

retentionDays.description: How long logs are kept, in days (a CloudWatch Logs retention value). Default: 30.

adminProtection.description: Admin protection (AWSManagedRulesAdminProtectionRuleSet): requests to admin-looking paths. Default: false.

anonymousIp.description: Anonymous IP list (AWSManagedRulesAnonymousIpList): VPNs, Tor, hosting providers. Suits B2B apps; too strict for most consumer apps. Default: false.

core.description: Core Rule Set (AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet): OWASP Top 10 — XSS, path traversal, remote file inclusion, SSRF. Default: true.

ipReputation.description: Amazon IP reputation list (AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList): IPs from Amazon threat intelligence. Default: true, or false when clientIpHeader is set.

knownBadInputs.description: Known bad inputs (AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet): Log4Shell, Java deserialisation, React RCE and other known exploit patterns. Default: true.

anvil:aws:WafMode.description: What WAF rules do when they match.

associationConfig.description: Specifies custom configurations for the associations between the web ACL and protected resources. See `association_config` below for details.

captchaConfig.description: Specifies how AWS WAF should handle CAPTCHA evaluations on the ACL level (used by [AWS Bot Control](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/aws-managed-rule-groups-bot.html)). See `captcha_config` below for details.

challengeConfig.description: Specifies how AWS WAF should handle Challenge evaluations on the ACL level (used by [AWS Bot Control](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/aws-managed-rule-groups-bot.html)). See `challenge_config` below for details.

customResponseBodies.description: Defines custom response bodies that can be referenced by `custom_response` actions. See `custom_response_body` below for details.

dataProtectionConfig.description: Specifies data protection to apply to the web request data for the web ACL. This is a web ACL level data protection option. See `data_protection_config` below for details.

defaultAction.description: Action to perform if none of the `rules` contained in the WebACL match. See `default_action` below for details.

name.description: Friendly name of the WebACL. If omitted, the provider will assign a random, unique name. Conflicts with `name_prefix`.

namePrefix.description: Creates a unique name beginning with the specified prefix. Conflicts with `name`.

region.description: Region where this resource will be [managed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#regional-endpoints). Defaults to the Region set in the provider configuration.

ruleJson.description: Raw JSON string to allow more than three nested statements. Conflicts with `rule` attribute. This is for advanced use cases where more than 3 levels of nested statements are required. **There is no drift detection at this time**. If you use this attribute instead of `rule`, you will be foregoing drift detection. Additionally, importing an existing web ACL into a configuration with `rule_json` set will result in a one time in-place update as the remote rule configuration is initially written to the `rule` attribute. See the AWS [documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/APIReference/API_CreateWebACL.html) for the JSON structure.

rules.description: Rule blocks used to identify the web requests that you want to `allow`, `block`, or `count`. See `rule` below for details.

scope.description: Specifies whether this is for an AWS CloudFront distribution or for a regional application. Valid values are `CLOUDFRONT` or `REGIONAL`. To work with CloudFront, you must also specify the region `us-east-1` (N. Virginia) on the AWS provider.

tags.description: Map of key-value pairs to associate with the resource. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.

tokenDomains.description: Specifies the domains that AWS WAF should accept in a web request token. This enables the use of tokens across multiple protected websites. When AWS WAF provides a token, it uses the domain of the AWS resource that the web ACL is protecting. If you don't specify a list of token domains, AWS WAF accepts tokens only for the domain of the protected resource. With a token domain list, AWS WAF accepts the resource's host domain plus all domains in the token domain list, including their prefixed subdomains.

visibilityConfig.description: Defines and enables Amazon CloudWatch metrics and web request sample collection. See `visibility_config` below for details.

enabled.description: Turns the rate limit on or off. Default: true.

limit.description: Maximum requests per client in each window (10 to 2,000,000,000). Default: 2000.

windowSeconds.description: Evaluation window in seconds: 60, 120, 300 or 600. Default: 300.
